_meta.purpose: Local, uncommitted permission allowlist for the two Suvarna execution sessions run unattended in /Users/Dev/suvarna/hq (Claude Code v2.1.239, --permission-mode dontAsk). Never committed: this file is .claude/settings.local.json, not .claude/settings.json.
findings_v2_1_239: permissions.allow/deny path rules for file tools only match on the canonical form Read(<glob>) or Edit(<glob>); Read(<glob>) governs Read/Glob/Grep/NotebookRead together, and Edit(<glob>) governs Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit together (confirmed via `claude --debug`: Write(<glob>), Glob(<glob>), MultiEdit(<glob>) and NotebookEdit(<glob>) are all logged as dead rules, 'not matched by file permission checks'). This template therefore never writes a Write(...) or Glob(...) path rule -- it would silently grant nothing.

Bash(<prefix> *) matches a Bash command by prefix, with the space before '*' significant (Bash(git status*) is a different, looser match than Bash(git status *)); a chained command (a && b) appears to require each segment to independently match an allow rule.

permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode is included per the L.15 brief but its effect could NOT be confirmed in this install: no lint/validation message appeared for it, but the settings loader also does not warn on entirely invented keys (checked with a nonsense key), so absence of a warning is not confirmation. The real enforcement in this template is structural: defaultMode is 'dontAsk' (never 'bypassPermissions'), and the deny list separately refuses any Bash invocation that itself tries to pass --dangerously-skip-permissions or a bypassPermissions mode. See INTERIM_RUNTIME_v1_0.md for the full account.
